cluster_name: Kyrenia-to-Turkey ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus with 267 aboard
tldr: At the headline layer all seventeen outlets converge on a minimal maritime-accident frame — ferry capsized, roughly 260–270 aboard, rescue underway — with almost no editorial differentiation across 11 country groups. Anadolu Agency (Turkey) is the sole outlet to lead with a named political actor ('TRNC premier confirms fatalities') rather than the event itself, making governmental authority the homepage-level hook. The Daily Mirror is the only outlet to deploy emotionally amplified language ('many feared dead') while The Independent uniquely foregrounds the rescue operation as the headline subject rather than the capsize. Wire-relay syndication is visible in near-identical phrasing shared by ARY News, Reuters, and Straits Times, all reproducing 'Boat with around 270 people on board capsizes off North Cyprus' with minimal adaptation.
event_summary: A passenger catamaran carrying 267 people capsized on August 30 a few kilometres off Kyrenia (Girne), northern Cyprus, shortly after departing for Tasucu, Turkey; TRNC Prime Minister Unal Ustel confirmed multiple fatalities, with at least 172 rescued and rescue operations ongoing.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use emotionally amplified language ('many feared dead') — all other outlets used neutral constructions such as 'fatalities reported', 'one dead', or no casualty language at all.

Only headline to foreground a named political actor (TRNC Prime Minister) as the grammatical subject, making governmental authority — not the maritime event — the top-level homepage hook; every other outlet led with the ship or the capsize.

Only headline to open with 'Rescue operation' as the subject, inverting the standard disaster-news structure and signalling a response-frame rather than an incident-frame visible at the RSS/homepage level.

bottom_line: The headline layer for this story is strikingly uniform: fifteen of seventeen outlets used near-identical accident-event language, compressing 267 passengers and an active rescue into 70-char factual summaries with almost no editorial voice. The two visible exceptions — Anadolu Agency's political-actor lead and the Daily Mirror's 'many feared dead' amplification — are register divergences, not substance divergences, confirming that headline-to-body framing divergence for this story is tonal rather than topical.
